    {"id":"c1","name":"Checkpoint modes","parent":"SQLite WAL checkpointing","neighborhood":"sub-concept","decision":"RESEARCH","reason":"Rel=5, Use=5, Nov=3, Int=4, Via=3, CVS=4.15: mode-specific waiting and completion semantics are useful missing refinements of existing WAL coverage."},
    {"id":"c2","name":"Checkpoint lock contention and busy handling","parent":"SQLite WAL checkpointing","neighborhood":"sub-concept","decision":"RESEARCH","reason":"Rel=5, Use=5, Nov=3, Int=4, Via=3, CVS=4.15: lock acquisition and fallback behavior directly affect checkpoint reliability."},
    {"id":"c3","name":"Checkpoint starvation","parent":"SQLite WAL checkpointing","neighborhood":"sub-concept","decision":"RESEARCH","reason":"Rel=5, Use=5, Nov=3, Int=4, Via=3, CVS=4.15: overlapping readers create an actionable checkpoint progress and WAL growth problem."},
    {"id":"c4","name":"Automatic checkpoint configuration","parent":"SQLite WAL checkpointing","neighborhood":"sub-concept","decision":"RESEARCH","reason":"Rel=5, Use=5, Nov=3, Int=3, Via=3, CVS=4.00: connection thresholds and disable conditions support concrete configuration decisions."},

    {"id":"c6","name":"WAL durability and synchronization ordering","parent":"SQLite transaction durability","neighborhood":"adjacent","decision":"RESEARCH","reason":"Rel=4, Use=5, Nov=3, Int=4, Via=2, CVS=3.75: synchronization modes and checkpoint ordering expose consequential durability requirements."},
    {"id":"c7","name":"WAL recycling and truncation","parent":"SQLite WAL checkpointing","neighborhood":"sub-concept","decision":"RESEARCH","reason":"Rel=5, Use=4, Nov=3, Int=3, Via=3, CVS=3.75: logical reuse and physical file shrinkage are distinct operational outcomes."},
    {"id":"c8","name":"Checkpoint progress telemetry","parent":"SQLite WAL checkpointing","neighborhood":"sub-concept","decision":"RESEARCH","reason":"Rel=5, Use=4, Nov=3, Int=3, Via=2, CVS=3.60: frame counters and their exceptional values support checkpoint monitoring."},
    {"id":"c9","name":"Reader end marks and snapshot visibility","parent":"SQLite WAL concurrency","neighborhood":"adjacent","decision":"RESEARCH","reason":"Rel=4, Use=4, Nov=3, Int=4, Via=2, CVS=3.50: reader snapshots explain the boundary that prevents checkpoint progress."},
    {"id":"c10","name":"WAL commit hooks","parent":"SQLite WAL integration APIs","neighborhood":"adjacent","decision":"RESEARCH","reason":"Rel=4, Use=4, Nov=3, Int=3, Via=3, CVS=3.50: hook replacement can silently change automatic checkpoint behavior."},
    {"id":"c11","name":"Checkpointing attached databases","parent":"SQLite WAL checkpointing","neighborhood":"sub-concept","decision":"RESEARCH","reason":"Rel=4, Use=4, Nov=3, Int=3, Via=2, CVS=3.35: database selection changes both error propagation and counter validity."},
    {"id":"c12","name":"Large write transactions and WAL growth","parent":"SQLite transaction sizing","neighborhood":"adjacent","decision":"RESEARCH","reason":"Rel=4, Use=4, Nov=3, Int=3, Via=2, CVS=3.35: transaction boundaries constrain when checkpointing can reset the WAL."},
    {"id":"c13","name":"WAL-index and shared-memory locality","parent":"SQLite WAL concurrency","neighborhood":"adjacent","decision":"RESEARCH","reason":"Rel=3, Use=4, Nov=3, Int=4, Via=2, CVS=3.25: the shared-memory index connects reader lookup performance with deployment constraints."},
    {"id":"c14","name":"Database crash recovery","parent":"SQLite","neighborhood":"parent","decision":"SKIP","reason":"Rel=3, Use=4, Nov=3, Int=4, Via=1, CVS=3.10: the packet supports the broader recovery context but cannot sustain its broad research scope."},
    {"id":"c15","name":"Rollback-journal recovery","parent":"Database crash recovery","neighborhood":"sibling","decision":"SKIP","reason":"Rel=3, Use=3, Nov=3, Int=3, Via=2, CVS=2.85: this alternative recovery mechanism is supported but less directly useful for checkpoint operations."}

  "claims": [
    {"id":"f1","concept_id":"c1","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting for database readers or writers to finish.","source_id":"S2","quote":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish","pass":0},
    {"id":"f2","concept_id":"c1","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL waits through the busy handler until there is no writer and all readers use the most recent snapshot.","source_id":"S2","quote":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f3","concept_id":"c1","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL blocks new writers while pending but permits new readers.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f4","concept_id":"c1","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART adds a wait for all readers to read only from the database file after checkpointing.","source_id":"S2","quote":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL with the addition that after checkpointing the log file it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback ) until all readers are reading from the database file only.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f5","concept_id":"c1","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE adds truncation of the log to zero bytes immediately before a successful return.","source_id":"S2","quote":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f6","concept_id":"c1","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP checkpoints zero frames and serves to obtain the checkpoint output counters.","source_id":"S2","quote":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f7","concept_id":"c2","text":"Concurrent checkpoint lock contention returns SQLITE_BUSY without invoking a configured busy handler.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f8","concept_id":"c2","text":"If the busy handler returns zero while waiting for the writer lock or readers, checkpointing falls back to SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE behavior.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE","pass":0},
    {"id":"f9","concept_id":"c2","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE never invokes the busy handler and can leave a checkpoint unfinished under concurrent readers or writers.","source_id":"S2","quote":"The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f10","concept_id":"c3","text":"If overlapping readers always leave at least one reader active, checkpoints cannot complete and the WAL grows without bound.","source_id":"S1","quote":"if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f11","concept_id":"c3","text":"Checkpoint starvation can be avoided by attempting checkpoints during reader gaps.","source_id":"S1","quote":"This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are \"reader gaps\": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f12","concept_id":"c4","text":"sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) triggers automatic checkpointing after a commit when the WAL contains at least N frames.","source_id":"S3","quote":"The sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) is a wrapper around sqlite3_wal_hook() that causes any database on database connection D to automatically checkpoint after committing a transaction if there are N or more frames in the write-ahead log file.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f13","concept_id":"c4","text":"Passing N less than or equal to zero disables automatic checkpoints.","source_id":"S3","quote":"Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f14","concept_id":"c4","text":"Every new database connection defaults to automatic checkpointing at 1000 pages or the SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT setting.","source_id":"S3","quote":"Every new database connection defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f15","concept_id":"c4","text":"The automatic checkpoint mechanism initiates PASSIVE checkpoints.","source_id":"S1","quote":"All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f16","concept_id":"c5","text":"The default automatic checkpoint runs in the thread performing the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.","source_id":"S1","quote":"By default, the checkpoint will be run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f17","concept_id":"c5","text":"Read performance deteriorates as WAL file size increases.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The wal-index helps find content in the WAL file much faster, but performance still falls off with increasing WAL file size.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f18","concept_id":"c5","text":"Infrequent checkpoints amortize checkpoint cost over more writes.","source_id":"S1","quote":"To maximize write performance, one wants to amortize the cost of each checkpoint over as many writes as possible, meaning that one wants to run checkpoints infrequently","pass":0},
    {"id":"f19","concept_id":"c6","text":"PRAGMA synchronous=FULL syncs the WAL on every transaction commit, whereas NORMAL omits that commit sync.","source_id":"S1","quote":"Writers sync the WAL on every transaction commit if PRAGMA synchronous is set to FULL but omit this sync if PRAGMA synchronous is set to NORMAL.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f20","concept_id":"c6","text":"The WAL must be synced to persistent storage before checkpointing moves its content into the database.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database","pass":0},
    {"id":"f21","concept_id":"c6","text":"The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.","source_id":"S1","quote":"the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL. Checkpoint also requires more seeking.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f22","concept_id":"c6","text":"With PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL, checkpointing is the only operation that issues an I/O barrier or sync operation.","source_id":"S1","quote":"Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation","pass":0},
    {"id":"f23","concept_id":"c7","text":"An ordinary checkpoint normally enables overwriting the WAL from the beginning rather than truncating it, unless journal_size_limit is set.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f24","concept_id":"c8","text":"pnLog reports the total WAL frame count, or -1 if checkpointing cannot run because of an error or non-WAL mode.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If pnLog is not NULL, then *pnLog is set to the total number of frames in the log file or to -1 if the checkpoint could not run because of an error or because the database is not in WAL mode","pass":0},
    {"id":"f25","concept_id":"c8","text":"pnCkpt includes frames checkpointed before the current function call.","source_id":"S2","quote":"*pnCkpt is set to the total number of checkpointed frames in the log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)","pass":0},
    {"id":"f26","concept_id":"c8","text":"A successful SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE sets both pnLog and pnCkpt to zero.","source_id":"S2","quote":"Note that upon successful completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE, the log file will have been truncated to zero bytes and so both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f27","concept_id":"c9","text":"A reader's end mark remains unchanged throughout its transaction, preserving a single point-in-time view.","source_id":"S1","quote":"for any particular reader, the end mark is unchanged for the duration of the transaction, thus ensuring that a single read transaction only sees the database content as it existed at a single point in time.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f28","concept_id":"c9","text":"A checkpoint must stop at a WAL page past any current reader's end mark.","source_id":"S1","quote":"the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f29","concept_id":"c10","text":"Registering a sqlite3_wal_hook callback disables automatic checkpointing configured through sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint.","source_id":"S3","quote":"Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f30","concept_id":"c11","text":"A NULL or empty zDb requests the operation on all attached WAL databases.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If parameter zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f31","concept_id":"c11","text":"When checkpointing all attached WAL databases, SQLITE_BUSY on one does not prevent attempts on the remaining databases.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If an SQLITE_BUSY error is encountered when processing one or more of the attached WAL databases, the operation is still attempted on any remaining attached databases and SQLITE_BUSY is returned at the end.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f32","concept_id":"c12","text":"The WAL cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.","source_id":"S1","quote":"A checkpoint can only complete when no other transactions are running, which means the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f33","concept_id":"c13","text":"The wal-index accelerates readers, but its shared-memory requirement places all readers on the same machine.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The wal-index greatly improves the performance of readers, but the use of shared memory means that all readers must exist on the same machine.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f34","concept_id":"c14","text":"Checkpoint synchronization is required to avoid possible database corruption after power loss or a hard reboot.","source_id":"S1","quote":"Checkpointing does require sync operations in order to avoid the possibility of database corruption following a power loss or hard reboot.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f35","concept_id":"c15","text":"Rollback-journal recovery restores original database content after a crash or ROLLBACK.","source_id":"S1","quote":"In the event of a crash or ROLLBACK , the original content contained in the rollback journal is played back into the database file to revert the database file to its original state.","pass":0}
  ],

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting for database readers or writers to finish.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL waits through the busy handler until there is no writer and all readers use the most recent snapshot.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL blocks new writers while pending but permits new readers.
claims.quote: This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART adds a wait for all readers to read only from the database file after checkpointing.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL with the addition that after checkpointing the log file it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback ) until all readers are reading from the database file only.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE adds truncation of the log to zero bytes immediately before a successful return.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP checkpoints zero frames and serves to obtain the checkpoint output counters.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.

claims.text: Concurrent checkpoint lock contention returns SQLITE_BUSY without invoking a configured busy handler.
claims.quote: If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.

claims.text: If the busy handler returns zero while waiting for the writer lock or readers, checkpointing falls back to SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE behavior.
claims.quote: If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE never invokes the busy handler and can leave a checkpoint unfinished under concurrent readers or writers.
claims.quote: The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers.

claims.text: If overlapping readers always leave at least one reader active, checkpoints cannot complete and the WAL grows without bound.
claims.quote: if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.

claims.text: Checkpoint starvation can be avoided by attempting checkpoints during reader gaps.
claims.quote: This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are "reader gaps": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.

claims.text: sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) triggers automatic checkpointing after a commit when the WAL contains at least N frames.
claims.quote: The sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) is a wrapper around sqlite3_wal_hook() that causes any database on database connection D to automatically checkpoint after committing a transaction if there are N or more frames in the write-ahead log file.

claims.text: Passing N less than or equal to zero disables automatic checkpoints.
claims.quote: Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.

claims.text: Every new database connection defaults to automatic checkpointing at 1000 pages or the SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT setting.
claims.quote: Every new database connection defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.

claims.text: The automatic checkpoint mechanism initiates PASSIVE checkpoints.
claims.quote: All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.

claims.text: The default automatic checkpoint runs in the thread performing the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.
claims.quote: By default, the checkpoint will be run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.

claims.text: Read performance deteriorates as WAL file size increases.
claims.quote: The wal-index helps find content in the WAL file much faster, but performance still falls off with increasing WAL file size.

claims.text: Infrequent checkpoints amortize checkpoint cost over more writes.
claims.quote: To maximize write performance, one wants to amortize the cost of each checkpoint over as many writes as possible, meaning that one wants to run checkpoints infrequently

claims.text: PRAGMA synchronous=FULL syncs the WAL on every transaction commit, whereas NORMAL omits that commit sync.
claims.quote: Writers sync the WAL on every transaction commit if PRAGMA synchronous is set to FULL but omit this sync if PRAGMA synchronous is set to NORMAL.

claims.text: The WAL must be synced to persistent storage before checkpointing moves its content into the database.
claims.quote: The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database

claims.text: The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.
claims.quote: the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL. Checkpoint also requires more seeking.

claims.text: With PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL, checkpointing is the only operation that issues an I/O barrier or sync operation.
claims.quote: Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation

claims.text: An ordinary checkpoint normally enables overwriting the WAL from the beginning rather than truncating it, unless journal_size_limit is set.
claims.quote: The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.

claims.text: pnLog reports the total WAL frame count, or -1 if checkpointing cannot run because of an error or non-WAL mode.
claims.quote: If pnLog is not NULL, then *pnLog is set to the total number of frames in the log file or to -1 if the checkpoint could not run because of an error or because the database is not in WAL mode

claims.text: pnCkpt includes frames checkpointed before the current function call.
claims.quote: *pnCkpt is set to the total number of checkpointed frames in the log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)

claims.text: A successful SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE sets both pnLog and pnCkpt to zero.
claims.quote: Note that upon successful completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE, the log file will have been truncated to zero bytes and so both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero.

claims.text: A reader's end mark remains unchanged throughout its transaction, preserving a single point-in-time view.
claims.quote: for any particular reader, the end mark is unchanged for the duration of the transaction, thus ensuring that a single read transaction only sees the database content as it existed at a single point in time.

claims.text: A checkpoint must stop at a WAL page past any current reader's end mark.
claims.quote: the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.

claims.text: Registering a sqlite3_wal_hook callback disables automatic checkpointing configured through sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint.
claims.quote: Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.

claims.text: A NULL or empty zDb requests the operation on all attached WAL databases.
claims.quote: If parameter zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db.

claims.text: When checkpointing all attached WAL databases, SQLITE_BUSY on one does not prevent attempts on the remaining databases.
claims.quote: If an SQLITE_BUSY error is encountered when processing one or more of the attached WAL databases, the operation is still attempted on any remaining attached databases and SQLITE_BUSY is returned at the end.

claims.text: The WAL cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.
claims.quote: A checkpoint can only complete when no other transactions are running, which means the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.

claims.text: The wal-index accelerates readers, but its shared-memory requirement places all readers on the same machine.
claims.quote: The wal-index greatly improves the performance of readers, but the use of shared memory means that all readers must exist on the same machine.

claims.text: Checkpoint synchronization is required to avoid possible database corruption after power loss or a hard reboot.
claims.quote: Checkpointing does require sync operations in order to avoid the possibility of database corruption following a power loss or hard reboot.

claims.text: Rollback-journal recovery restores original database content after a crash or ROLLBACK.
claims.quote: In the event of a crash or ROLLBACK , the original content contained in the rollback journal is played back into the database file to revert the database file to its original state.
